big_idea: We can SORT everyday events into THREE likelihood buckets: impossible, possible, certain.
learning_intention: We are learning to sort events into three likelihood groups.
student_learning_goal: I can sort events into three likelihood groups.
success_criteria: I can place an event in the IMPOSSIBLE bucket.
I can place an event in the POSSIBLE bucket.
I can place an event in the CERTAIN bucket.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Lucky and Mae — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Lesson 2 sort tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Mae: I have a PILE of events. Help me put each one in the right bucket: IMPOSSIBLE, POSSIBLE, or CERTAIN! Mae opens: 'Will it? Maybe!' Class: 'Impossible — Possible — Certain!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Lucky and Mae puppets. 'Friends — yesterday we learned the 3 likelihood words. Today we SORT a big pile of events.'

Review vocabulary. 'Impossible = never. Possible = maybe. Certain = always.'

Demonstrate the sort. Show the 3-zone mat (left=IMPOSSIBLE, middle=POSSIBLE, right=CERTAIN). Place a card: 'A dog will speak words today.' Goes in IMPOSSIBLE. 'It will rain at recess.' Goes in POSSIBLE. 'Lunch will be served today.' Goes in CERTAIN.

More examples — children call out the bucket:
- 'Snow falls in summer.' (IMPOSSIBLE)
- 'I will see a friend smile.' (POSSIBLE)
- 'School ends today.' (CERTAIN)
- 'A ladybug will land on my hand.' (POSSIBLE)
- 'I will turn 10 today.' (depends on age — usually IMPOSSIBLE for G1)
- 'The clock will tick.' (CERTAIN)

'Mae says — every event has ONE bucket. Pick the bucket. Place the card.'

'Today we sort 24 events into 3 buckets.'
student_actions: Practice placing cards on a 3-zone mat.

steps.instruction: Whole group: sort 6 events on a giant 3-zone mat as a class.
Three stations. Station A: Sort 12 cards (4 of each bucket). Station B: 'Hard sorts' — 8 ambiguous events that need discussion. Station C: Make Your Own — pair invents 6 events and sorts them.
Stretch challenge at Station B: justify each placement with WHY ('possible because it sometimes happens at recess').
Discuss tricky 'possible' events. 'POSSIBLE means it MIGHT happen. Sun shining at noon = certain in summer, possible in winter (might be cloudy).'
steps.teacher_prompt: Show 2 tricky events and reason aloud.

steps.instruction: Circulate to record formative evidence on the sort tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Why is this in CERTAIN?' Mark the tracker.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: 2 pairs share their sorted bins. Class compares disputed cards and votes — what evidence puts a card in CERTAIN vs POSSIBLE? Frame in Jones et al. (1997) Level 2 terms: children must justify the bin with cause-effect reasoning, not feeling.
steps.teacher_prompt: Mae: 'Same card, different bin? Tell me WHY. Math chance is about REASONS, not feelings.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Use only the obvious-impossible and obvious-certain cards.
differentiation.for_extending: Stretch at Station B with 'why' explanations.
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Provide a sentence frame: 'This is ___ because ___.'
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Children physically walk to 3 corners (impossible/possible/certain) when teacher reads an event.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: sorts impossible correctly; sorts possible correctly; sorts certain correctly.

discussion_prompts: Are there events that change buckets in different seasons?
consolidation.exit_routine: Mae's call-and-response refrain — Mae calls 'Will it? Maybe!' and class chants back 'Impossible — Possible — Certain!' Repeat 3x. Each child sticks ONE event-card to the right bin on the wall chart.

assessment_in_this_lesson.evidence_collected: Sorting accuracy across all 3 likelihood categories.
assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 2 captures D2.1 mastery for sorting events by likelihood.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child sorts SILLY events as POSSIBLE — repairing the silly-not-impossible trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
When children sort events by likelihood, the dominant Grade-1 trap is the equiprobability bias — every outcome feels equally likely because it's all 'chance' (Fischbein 1975, 'The Intuitive Sources of Probabilistic Thinking in Children'). Jones, Langrall & Thornton (1997) Level-1-to-2 transition frames this as the move from 'anything could happen' to ordered IMPOSSIBLE → POSSIBLE → CERTAIN. Today's three-bin sort drives that ordering.

Lesson 1 named the three categories; today we sort within them. Lesson 3 will use the sort to PREDICT, and Lesson 4 will TEST those predictions.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station A. Card: 'A pig will fly to school today.' Child places it in POSSIBLE. Says 'maybe!'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You put this in POSSIBLE. But Lucky asks — CAN pigs fly? Like, in real life?'

Child says 'no'. 'Right. Pigs CANNOT fly. So this is IMPOSSIBLE — it CANNOT happen.'

Walk through. 'POSSIBLE means it COULD happen. IMPOSSIBLE means it CANNOT — there's a real-world reason.'

'Pigs can't fly because they have no wings. That's an impossible reason. Snow in July in Toronto — too warm. Impossible.'

Generalise. 'Lucky says — ask yourself: COULD this really happen in our world? Yes = possible/certain. No = impossible.'

Now re-sort. Card: 'I will turn into a fish.' Impossible. Card: 'My friend will smile at me.' Possible.

If still using POSSIBLE: provide a 'reality check' question card: 'CAN this really happen?' Force the test.

Long-term recovery: every sort asks 'is this real-world possible?'
expected_student_responses: (Strong) Sorts independently using real-world possibility test.
common_misconceptions: Anything imaginable is possible. (Repair: real-world possible only.)
Silly = impossible. (Repair: silly events can be possible if real.)
Hard to do = impossible. (Repair: hard but doable = possible.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child sorts everything as POSSIBLE: pose three obviously-impossible events ('a fish will fly to the moon today') and three obviously-certain events ('we will breathe air'); child anchors those before tackling middle cases.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child sorts CERTAIN as POSSIBLE: drill 'must-happen' test — 'is it locked-in or just likely?' If locked, CERTAIN.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child swaps IMPOSSIBLE and POSSIBLE: introduce a physical sorting hoop; impossible cards must NEVER touch the centre (possible) hoop. Spatial separation prevents accidental swaps.

parts_outline.task: Read 6 events. Write I, P, or C.
Make a tricky event for EACH category. Why does it fit?

expected_image_assets: 3 blank event lines + reason boxes for Part 3
